description: A sample-based tabla machine: twelve named strokes on buttons and jacks, plus stored traditional patterns played from a clock

params.text: Steps forward through the stored patterns, despite the maker's tooltip calling it Prev Theka
Steps back through the stored patterns, despite the maker's tooltip calling it Next Theka
Picks how a stroke's several samples are used: one fixed sample every time, each of them in turn, or one at random

inputs.text: A rising edge past 2V plays the Dha stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Dhin stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Dhit stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Dhun stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Ga stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Ge stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Ke stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Na stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Ta stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Ti stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Tin stroke
A rising edge past 2V plays the Tun stroke
Plays the next beat of the selected pattern on each rising edge past 2V
A rising edge past 2V sends the pattern back to its first beat
While this is high the strokes you trigger are accented; it is ignored while a pattern is playing
A rising edge past 2V picks one of the stored patterns at random

outputs.text: The left side of the tabla mix
The right side of the tabla mix

notes: the strokes play on their own, but the stored patterns need a clock patched before anything runs
the display names the pattern and shows its beats, and it carries no control that can be clicked for help
PLY lights while a pattern is running, SAM on the first beat of the cycle and ACC on an accented beat
a pattern stops being treated as running once no clock has arrived for about as long as the last gap between clocks
